title: Status of the World's Soil Resources
topic: soil organic carbon, soil health and water retention
text: The FAO and Intergovernmental Technical Panel on Soils report identifies soil organic carbon decline and soil degradation as global threats. Maintaining soil organic matter and protecting soil from degradation are central soil-health practices.

title: The State of the World's Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture
topic: agricultural biodiversity, diversification and ecosystem services
text: FAO documents the contribution of biodiversity for food and agriculture to ecosystem services and describes the importance of diverse species, habitats and management practices in production systems.

title: Climate Change and Land: Summary for Policymakers
topic: heat, drought, land degradation and adaptation
text: The IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Land assesses interactions among climate change, land degradation, desertification, food security and sustainable land management, including risks from warming and water stress.

title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
text: The IPBES Global Assessment identifies changes in land and sea use, including habitat loss and fragmentation, among the direct drivers affecting nature.

title: Making Peace With Nature
text: UNEP synthesizes evidence on climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution, emphasizing that these environmental crises are interconnected and require coordinated action.

title: State of Knowledge of Soil Biodiversity
topic: soil biodiversity and sustainable soil management
text: FAO summarizes the functions of soil organisms and the links between soil biodiversity, ecosystem functioning and sustainable soil management.

title: Riparian Zone and Stream Restoration
topic: riparian restoration, stream habitat and bank stability
text: US EPA describes riparian-zone restoration as a way to improve fish habitat, stabilize stream banks, and support stream and water-quality restoration.

title: Nonpoint Source: Agriculture
topic: agricultural runoff, nutrients, pesticides and river water quality
text: US EPA explains that agricultural runoff can transport sediment, nutrients, pesticides, and other pollutants to rivers and streams, with risks to aquatic life and water quality.

title: Factsheet on Water Quality Parameters, Habitat Assessment
topic: stream habitat, flow, runoff and aquatic condition
text: US EPA identifies flow, habitat condition, and runoff from urban and agricultural areas as factors that can affect aquatic and riparian habitat quality.
